requirements.requirement: On SIGHUP, writer.py must reopen the current audit.log, release the previous file descriptor, and continue writing without restarting.
requirements.summary: A bounded rotation test preserved PID 3489 and start_ticks 22838, showed the rotated file stop at 656 bytes, showed the new audit.log grow from 48 to 80 bytes, and found only the current audit.log held open.

requirements.requirement: writer.py must close its log and exit cleanly on SIGTERM.
requirements.summary: After SIGTERM the process disappeared, audit.log remained stable at 240 bytes, and a system-wide descriptor scan found no holders under the recovery directory. Equivalent behavior was observed again after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Existing archive records must be preserved.
requirements.summary: archive/previous.log contained the original A100 record before modification and retained the same SHA-1 checksum and content through the completed work and reboot.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The repaired source compiled with Python 2.4.3. CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were observed before and after reboot, with the fixed lifecycle platform snapshots also unchanged.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct runtime evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also substantially complete: node1 had a pre-restart identity and validated source/data state, acknowledged the restart, returned with a different boot identity corroborated by the lifecycle snapshots, retained matching files and platform state, and passed post-reboot signal behavior. Hygiene is reduced by an initially stray test writer and several retained test artifacts.
limitations: The deleted-file scenario was exercised through rename-based rotation rather than unlinking the open file; the descriptor scan and stable rotated-file size nevertheless directly demonstrate release of the old descriptor.

No managed init service or cluster was configured, so restart recovery was demonstrated through node health, persisted source/data, and manually launched runtime tests rather than service-manager or cluster-state probes.

The lifecycle package-health command is unsupported by this legacy yum version, and systemd service-state collection is unavailable on CentOS 5; therefore those supplemental checks cannot independently establish package or service health.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Core changes were scoped and no package, socket, OS, kernel, or persistent service changes were observed. The first timed-out launch was an unnecessary failed test mutation that left a stray writer; it was fully stopped by cmd-9d5eb47cb4d54b91. The first contaminated rotation attempt was superseded and did not establish the final result; its audit-before-sighup.log artifact remained (cmd-b0d77156d2244898, cmd-44d4697139314a3d). The valid second rotation also left audit-second-before-sighup.log rather than cleaning the test artifact (cmd-590f4f0b4b064128, cmd-cc763d7d38554154). Verification PID, output, and bytecode files remained under /tmp from the launch and compilation commands. These were low-risk but unwanted residue.
